BENECON111.name: Introduction to Economics
BENECON111.role: covers introductory microeconomics and macroeconomics together (supply and demand, game theory, consumer and firm theory, aggregate output and inflation)

BENECON211.name: International Macroeconomics
BENECON211.role: examines national income, growth, unemployment, business cycles, international trade and fiscal/monetary policy

BENECON212.name: Microeconomics & Behavior
BENECON212.role: deepens consumer behaviour, market structure and behavioural microeconomics beyond the Year-1 introduction

BENECON311.name: Public Economics
BENECON311.role: examines market failure, public goods, taxation, redistribution and political economy

BENECON312.name: Econometrics
BENECON312.role: OLS/GLS/IV, tests and an empirical Stata paper develop quantitative economic enquiry; VU MethodsII R/RStudio and full integrated methods sequence remain distinct.

BENECON314.name: Behavioral Economics
BENECON314.role: integrates psychological insight -- biases, heuristics, framing -- into economic decision-making

BENGATE102.name: Research Methods & Statistics
BENGATE102.role: is the general introduction to research design, operationalisation, sampling and inferential statistics

DISARIN212.name: Logic & Discrete Mathematics
DISARIN212.role: Formal logic, proofs and discrete mathematics support rigorous reasoning; this is not philosophy of science, full decision theory or epistemology.

DISGATE102.name: Mathematical Methods
DISGATE102.role: trains the calculus, algebra and problem-solving techniques grounding PPE's own mathematics-heavy first-year economics and admission requirements

DISMATH214.name: Advanced Calculus
DISMATH214.role: extends calculus to multiple dimensions and differential equations, deepening PPE's mathematics-heavy quantitative training

DISMATH314.name: Probability & Statistics
DISMATH314.role: provides a rigorous foundation in probability theory and statistical inference, extending PPE's methods training toward advanced quantitative work

GOSGATE102.name: Law, Society & Justice
GOSGATE102.role: Legal, social and normative foundations complement governance enquiry; no transaction-cost policy project or integrated PPE Practice equivalence.

GOSHIST111.name: Modern History
GOSHIST111.role: gives a chronological overview of the political ideals -- popular sovereignty, nationalism, the rise of industrial societies -- that ground comparative and institutional study of politics

GOSHIST211.name: History of Empires
GOSHIST211.role: examines great powers and the historical exercise of power politics, complementing PPE's own attention to power, conflict and political institutions

GOSLAWJ111.name: Human Rights: Law & Philosophy
GOSLAWJ111.role: Human-rights law, history and philosophical argument provide a partial rights-based global-justice contribution, not the complete external elective.

GOSLAWJ212.name: Introduction to Public International Law
GOSLAWJ212.role: Public international law supplies legal analysis of international order, not a replacement for integrated ConnectedWorld applications.

GOSLAWJ213.name: Comparative Constitutional Law
GOSLAWJ213.role: compares the constitutional law of five legal systems, examining the institutional design that structures political power

GOSPHIL111.name: Introduction to Western Philosophy
GOSPHIL111.role: Western philosophical questions, historical ideas and argument ground later philosophy; no exact VU reading-list or HistoryII equivalence.

GOSPHIL212.name: Ethics
GOSPHIL212.role: Virtue ethics, deontology and utilitarianism provide substantive normative reasoning; partial ethics overlap.

GOSPHIL214.name: Philosophy of Mind
GOSPHIL214.role: Consciousness, personal identity and the mind-body problem deepen philosophical enquiry; they do not stand in for epistemology.

GOSPHIL311.name: Philosophy of Emotion
GOSPHIL311.role: examines the philosophical study of emotion, affect and rationality, extending the Philosophy specialisation's treatment of the person's evaluative life beyond its four instantiated electives

GOSPHIL313.name: Free Will, Time & the Self
GOSPHIL313.role: Free will, personal identity, agency and time deepen responsibility questions; partial overlap with autonomy/ethics, not the full external syllabus.

GOSPOLI111.name: Introduction to Political Philosophy
GOSPOLI111.role: Normative arguments about political authority, rights and the state provide a substantive foundation for PPE political philosophy.

GOSPOLI112.name: Foundations of Comparative Politics
GOSPOLI112.role: Empirical comparative analysis of political systems, democracy and institutional change provides substantive comparative-politics training.

GOSPOLI212.name: Theory of International Relations
GOSPOLI212.role: gives a historical and contemporary grounding in international relations and geopolitics, supporting the Politics specialisation's international-relations territory

GOSPOLI311.name: European Union Politics
GOSPOLI311.role: examines the European Union's decision-making rules, actors and policy-making, supporting the Politics specialisation's EU-institutions territory

GOSPOLI312.name: Public Policy Analysis
GOSPOLI312.role: Studies how public policy is framed and made across national and international arenas through a sugar case and policy memos, complementing the public-choice focus without reproducing integrated PPE practice.

GOSPOLI313.name: Peace & Conflict
GOSPOLI313.role: analyses the causes, dynamics and resolution of violent and nonviolent conflict, supporting the Politics specialisation's international-security territory

GOSSOCI111.name: Introduction to Sociology
GOSSOCI111.role: provides the general toolkit for understanding how societies function locally and globally, supporting PPE's own emphasis on evaluating solutions to urgent societal challenges through combined disciplinary lenses

GOSSOCI212.name: Qualitative Research Methodology
GOSSOCI212.role: Qualitative design and interview-based enquiry provide partial methods overlap; no identical political research design/software or supervised thesis is assumed.

GOSSOCI214.name: Modern Sociology
GOSSOCI214.role: examines the trajectory of sociology and debates about modernity, extending the societal-problem-solving strand beyond the introductory course

GOSSOCI215.name: Social Movements & Environmental Justice
GOSSOCI215.role: Level2 study of environmental-justice movements adds a contemporary social application; it is not VU advanced growth/development modelling capstone.

MCCCOMM311.name: Persuasive Communication
MCCCOMM311.role: Ethical persuasion and communication in science/society/sustainability complement public argument; community application does not guarantee a named future partner.

alternatives.assessment: The closest response retains five philosophy and six economics courses, political foundations and mathematical, formal and social research. Public Policy Analysis is an applied complement, using a sugar case and policy memos. It does not replace VU’s interdisciplinary sequence.

The political-economy option retains five politics and six economics courses. Constitutional and international law address institutions directly. Modern History and History of Empires give specific historical grounding in sovereignty, industrialisation and imperial institutions. Ethics remains in term 2, IR precedes EU Politics and Peace & Conflict.

The Philosophy and Politics option retains five dedicated philosophy and five politics courses, with human rights, international law and comparative constitutional law. Introduction to Economics remains the only economics course. Its schedule passes unchanged.

stopping: All three options pass; maximum reached. Relative weights change rather than merely substituting labels. Examples and postgraduate or career interests do not create another route.

alignment.rationale: Both introduce inference and regression with R. VU focuses on empirical PPE questions and introductory econometrics, while UCR also covers survey and experimental design.
Partial calculus/optimisation foundation; VU additionally teaches formal logic, game/social-choice theory and compulsory MathLabs.
Partial introduction to Western philosophical ideas and argument; not an identical historical reading sequence.
Partial normative-ethics overlap through virtue ethics, deontology and utilitarianism.
Partial philosophical agency/free-will contribution; not the complete autonomy and responsibility syllabus.
Partial rights-based philosophical/legal contribution to global justice.
Both study normative political theory, including authority and rights. VU develops this work in a specialist second-year course.
Formal logic does not reproduce philosophy of science.
VU continues the historical study of philosophical texts beyond its first-year course.
VU introduces empirical approaches to the state, power and conflict. UCR’s political philosophy course aligns with the more directly related VU political theory course.
Partial comparative-systems and institutional-change overlap, with empirical political enquiry.
Partial introductory microeconomics; this combined micro/macro course is not counted twice as two complete external units.
UCR’s introductory course covers both microeconomics and macroeconomics and appears alongside the VU microeconomics course. VU gives each subject its own introductory course.
Partial consumer/market/behavioural microeconomics overlap; exact external formal methods are not reproduced.
Partial macroeconomic growth, cycles and policy overlap; no full external syllabus equivalence.
VU offers a dedicated course in international trade and development. UCR’s International Macroeconomics covers related open-economy questions.
VU brings ethics, politics and economics together to study wellbeing and markets in a dedicated course.
VU continues its interdisciplinary application sequence in a dedicated second course.
Both examine market failure and public policy. VU makes transaction costs and institutional analysis central to an interdisciplinary policy project.
Integrated moral, political and economic problem analysis is not reproduced by public international law.
Current VU capstone integrates growth/development models, moral valuation, ecological and catastrophic-risk critiques; UCR level2 environmental movements is a companion topic, not this capstone.
Partial qualitative design/interview overlap; the VU political-research and dedicated software trajectory is not identical.
VU students develop a literature review and research proposal in a supervised tutorial that leads into the thesis.
The illustrated VU route includes 30 EC of approved courses at a partner university.
VU requires a 12 EC individual thesis. UCR optional independent research sits outside the scheduled 180 EC.
